messages.content: Write a short scene in modern American English about two longtime adult friends walking home together after school. They are still on the way home. Keep them walking and talking throughout the scene. Do not have them arrive home, enter a house, get into a car, or change locations. Do not introduce any other characters. Let the scene end naturally while they are still walking.

“You know what I hate?”

Alex glanced over. “Your long list of things you hate?”

“Besides that.”

“Okay. What?”

“When people say, ‘It could be worse.’”

Alex made a face. “Yeah. That's not exactly comforting.”

“Right? You tell someone you had a terrible day and they hit you with, ‘Well, at least nobody died.’”

“That is a spectacularly low bar.”

“Exactly.”

They kept walking, falling into step again after Alex drifted toward the grass to avoid a crack in the sidewalk.

“So what would you rather hear?” she asked.

Jordan thought about it. “Honestly? ‘That sucks.’”

Alex laughed. “That's your ideal emotional support?”

“It's honest.”

“You're impossible.”

“And yet you keep hanging out with me.”

“Bad judgment.”

“Clearly.”

Alex bumped her shoulder against Jordan's, and Jordan bumped her back a little harder.

“Hey.”

“You started it.”

“I absolutely did not.”

“You absolutely did.”

Jordan shook her head, smiling as they continued down the sidewalk. Neither of them was in any particular hurry. They had a few more blocks to go, and plenty of time to argue about nothing.”
